caption: The Ninnion Tablet, a votive plaque depicting the Eleusinian Mysteries (4th century BC, National Archaeological Museum, Athens).
alt: Terracotta votive plaque shaped like a small temple, painted with rows of robed figures, some carrying torches and sheaves, arranged in a procession before seated goddesses; a dedicatory inscription runs along the bottom edge.
credit: Photo by Marsyas / Wikimedia Commons. National Archaeological Museum, Athens.
note: Clement's text survives only as a Wikisource transcription (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. II), with no accompanying images; the one Internet Archive scan of that exact volume found (antenicenefather0000unse_k3i9) is a restricted lending-library item with no accessible page images. The Ninnion Tablet is a genuine ancient artifact directly depicting Eleusinian initiation rites, the same rites Clement describes and mocks in this excerpt, chosen over a modern illustration per the brief's guidance.
